source: Confucius said: There are seventy-seven disciples who have studied with me and become proficient in the six arts. They are all people with extraordinary talents. Outstanding in virtue: Yan Yuan, Min Ziqian, Ran Boniu, Zhong Gong. Those who are good at handling political affairs: Ran You, Ji Lu. In terms of language: Zaiwo, Zigong. Articles on erudition: Ziyou, Zixia. Master Zhuan Sun was extreme, Zeng Shen was slow, Gao Chai was stupid, Zhong You was rude, and Yan Hui was often poor and had nothing. Duanmuci did not accept the mercy of fate and went into business, but his predictions on the market were often accurate. The people whom Confucius respected: in the Zhou Dynasty, it was Laozi; in the Wei Kingdom, it was Zang Boyu; in the Qi Kingdom, it was Yan Zhongping; in the Chu Kingdom, it was Laolaizi; in the Zheng Kingdom, it was Zichan; in the Lu Kingdom, it was Meng Gongchuo. He also often praised Zang Wenzhong, Liu Xiahui, Tongtan Bohua, and Jieshan Ziran. Confucius was born later than them and was not of the same era. Yan Hui was from the state of Lu, his courtesy name was Ziyuan. Thirty years younger than Confucius. Yan Yuan asked what benevolence was, and Confucius said: Restrain yourself and make your words and deeds conform to etiquette, and people in the world will praise you as a virtuous person. Confucius said: Yan Hui! What a virtuous person! He ate a small bamboo basket of rice, drank a ladle of water, and lived in a simple alley. Most people couldn't bear this kind of hardship, but Yan Hui didn't change his joy. When he was listening to my teachings, Yan Hui seemed like a stupid person. After class, I examined his private conversations and showed that he was able to express himself deliberately. Yan Hui was really not stupid. When you are employed, you will save the world; when you are not employed, you will hide your secrets. Only you and I have such an attitude towards life! Yan Hui was only twenty-nine years old, his hair turned completely white, and he died prematurely. Confucius cried very sadly and said: Since I had Yan Hui, the students have become closer and closer to me. Duke Ai of Lu asked: Who among the students is the best at learning? Confucius replied: There is a man named Yan Hui who had better learn from others and never transfer his anger to others and never make the same mistake again. Unfortunately, life was short, and after death, there are no such people anymore. Min Sun, also known as Ziqian, was fifteen years younger than Confucius. Confucius said: Min Ziqian is too filial! He serves his parents and obeys his brothers. Others praise him without any criticism. He does not want to be a retainer of a high official, and he does not want to receive a salary from an emperor. So he said: If someone calls me again, I will definitely flee to the north of Wenshui River. Ran Geng, courtesy name Boniu. Confucius thought he was virtuous. Boniu was suffering from an incurable disease. Confucius went to greet him, shook his hand from the window, and said: This is life! Such a good person got such a disease, what a fate! Ran Yong, courtesy name Zhong Gong. Zhong Gong asked how to handle political affairs. Confucius said: When going out to do things, be as courteous and courteous as receiving distinguished guests, and use the people as piously and cautiously as hosting a grand ceremony. In this way, no one will resent you if you serve in the feudal state of a prince, and no one will resent you if you serve in the home of a high official.

Yan Hui died prematurely at twenty-nine, causing Confucius great grief. Duke Ai of Lu was told Yan Hui was the best learner, never transferring anger or repeating mistakes.

source: Confucius thought that Zhong Gong had achieved great achievements in virtue and said: Ran Yong, you can make him a high official like a senior official. Zhong Gong's father was a man of humble status. Confucius used an analogy and said: A mottled cow gives birth to a red calf with round and straight horns. Even if you don't want to use it as a sacrifice, will the gods of the mountains and rivers abandon it? Ran Qiu, also known as Zi You, was twenty-nine years younger than Confucius. As the head of Li family's retainers. Ji Kangzi asked Confucius: Is Ran Qiu virtuous? Confucius replied: There is a city with a thousand households and a fief with a hundred chariots. Ran Qiu can manage the military and political affairs there well. As for whether he is benevolent or not, I don't know. Ji Kangzi asked again: Is Zilu virtuous? Confucius replied: Just like Ran Qiu. Ran Qiu asked Confucius: Do you act immediately when you hear what you should do? Confucius replied: Act immediately. Zilu asked Confucius: When you hear something you should do, should you act immediately? Confucius replied: How can you act immediately when you hear something when your father and brothers are here? Zihua felt that this was strange and said in confusion: "I boldly ask, why do you ask the same question but get different answers?" Confucius replied: Ran Qiu was timid and worried, so I encouraged him. Zhong Yu has the courage of two people to do things, so I have to restrain him. Zhong Yuan, named Zi Lu, was from Bian. Nine years younger than Confucius. Zilu had a rough temperament, liked to show off his strength, had a strong ambition, and was straightforward. He wore a rooster-style hat and a sword decorated with boar skin. He once bullied Confucius. Confucius slowly induced him with ritual music. Later, Zilu dressed in Confucian clothes and brought a gift for apprenticeship. Through the recommendation of Confucius's students, Zilu asked to be Confucius's student. Zilu asked how to deal with political affairs. Confucius said: You must first set an example for the people, and then you can make the people work hard. Zilu asked for further explanation. Confucius said: Be persistent. Zilu asked: Does a gentleman value bravery? Confucius said: What a gentleman values ​​most is righteousness. A gentleman who has no choice but to be brave but does not uphold righteousness will become rebellious and rebellious. A villain who has no choice but to be brave but not uphold righteousness will become a robber. Zi Lu wanted to hear some truth, but he didn't act immediately, for fear of hearing another truth. Confucius said: The only person who can decide a case by just listening to one side's words is Zhong You! Zhong Yu advocates bravery more than I can use it, so it does not apply. People with a temperament like Zhongyou's will not end well. I'm afraid Zhong You is the only one who doesn't feel ashamed to stand next to people wearing fur coats while wearing a shabby robe made of tangled linen. Zhong Yuan's knowledge seems to have reached the main hall, but he has not yet been able to enter the inner room. Ji Kangzi asked: Is Zhong You virtuous? Confucius replied: A country with a thousand chariots can let him manage military and political affairs. As for whether he has benevolence, I don't know. Zilu liked to travel with Confucius and met hermits such as Changju, Jieyou, and an old man carrying farm tools. Zilu became Ji's retainer. Ji Sun asked Confucius: Can Zilu be said to be a retainer? Confucius replied: It can be said that he is a minister who is ready to fill his position. Zilu was appointed as the official of Pucheng and bid farewell to Confucius. Confucius said: There are many brave warriors in Pu Yi, and it is difficult to govern them. However, I tell you: if you are respectful and humble, you can control brave people; if you are generous and honest, you can bring everyone close to you; if you are respectful and honest and the society is quiet, you can use it to serve your superiors. At first, Duke Linggong of Wei had a favorite concubine named Nanzi.

source: King Wu was very happy, so he sent Zigong to Yue. The King of Yue cleared the road and went to the outskirts to greet Zigong. He personally drove his car to the residence where Zigong was staying and asked, "This is a remote and backward country. Why did the doctor humiliate his solemn status and come here?" Zigong replied: Now I have persuaded King Wu to rescue Lu and attack Qi. He wanted to do this but was afraid of Yue and said, "Wait until I capture Yue." Like this, it is inevitable to conquer the Yue Kingdom. Besides, it would be too clumsy to make people suspicious of someone without the intention to retaliate; it would be unsafe to have people know about it if he has the intention to seek revenge; it would be too dangerous to let people know about it before the matter has started. These three situations are the biggest disaster in getting things done. After hearing this, Gou Jian kowtowed to the ground and bowed again and said: I once overestimated my capabilities and went to war with Wu. I was besieged in Kuaiji. I hated him so much that my lips were parched day and night. I only wanted to fight to the death with the King of Wu. This is my wish. So he asked Zigong what to do. Zigong said: The king of Wu was ferocious and cruel, and the ministers could not bear it; the country fought many wars, which made it exhausted and decayed, and the soldiers could not bear it; the people resented the king, and there were internal disturbances among the ministers; Wu Zixu was killed for his remonstrances, and the chief minister came to power, complied with the fault of the king, and used it to protect his own selfish interests. This is a political manifestation of harming the country. Now if the king can really send troops to assist the king of Wu, appeal to his will, use heavy gold and treasures to win his favor, and honor him with humble words to show respect for him, he will definitely attack Qi. If that war cannot be won, it will be your great blessing. If he wins, he will definitely lead his troops to approach Jin. Please let me go north to meet the king of Jin and let him attack it together. This will definitely weaken the power of Wu. When all their elite troops were consumed in the Qi State, the heavy troops were restrained by the Jin State, and the king took advantage of its exhaustion to attack it, which would surely destroy the Wu State. The King of Yue was very happy and agreed to act according to the plan. He gave Zigong a hundred yi of gold, a precious sword, and two good spears. Zigong didn't accept it and left. Zigong reported back to the King of Wu and said: I solemnly told the King of Yue what you said. The King of Yue was very frightened and said: I am very unlucky. I lost my father when I was young. Five days later, Wen Zhong, a senior official from the State of Yue, kowtowed to the ground and said to the King of Wu: Gou Jian, the minister of the East China Sea Service, would like to send the envoy Wen Zhong to repair your subordinates and ask them to send greetings to the king. Now I heard privately that the king is going to launch an army of justice to attack the violent, support the weak and tyrannical Qi State and appease the Zhou royal family. I request to send out the entire army of 3,000 people in Yue State. Gou Jian requested to personally wear armor and carry sharp weapons, and was willing to risk the danger of arrows and stones in front. Therefore, Wen Zhong, a humble minister of the Yue Kingdom, was sent to present the treasures treasured by his ancestors, including twelve pieces of armor, axes, Qulu spears, and light swords, as gifts to the noble military officials. The King of Wu was very happy after hearing this and told Zigong what Wen Zhong had said: The King of Yue wants to follow me personally to attack Qi. Is that okay? Zigong replied: No. It is unethical to make someone else's country empty, mobilize all his troops, and ask his king to follow him on an expedition. You accept his gift and allow him to send his army without his king accompanying him. The king of Wu agreed and thanked the king of Yue. So King Wu mobilized the troops from nine counties to attack Qi. Zigong therefore left the state of Wu and went to the state of Jin. He said to the king of Jin: I heard that if you don't plan a strategy in advance, you can't cope with sudden changes, and if you don't manage the army well in advance, you can't defeat the enemy. Now the state of Qi and the state of Wu are about to go to war. If the state of Wu cannot win the war, the state of Yue will definitely take the opportunity to disrupt it; after winning the battle with the state of Qi, the king of Wu will definitely lead his army to approach the state of Jin. Jin was very panicked and said: What should we do? Zigong said: Prepare your weapons, recuperate your soldiers, and wait for the arrival of the Wu army. Jin Jun did as he said. Zigong left Jin and went to Lu. Sure enough, the King of Wu fought a battle with the Qi people in Ailing and defeated the Qi army. He captured seven generals' soldiers and refused to return home. Sure enough, he led his troops to approach the Jin state and met the Jin people in Huangchi. Wu and Jin were competing for supremacy. The Jin people attacked Wu and defeated the Wu army. When the King of Yue heard the news of the Wu army's disastrous defeat, he crossed the river to attack the state of Wu. He did not set up camp until he was seven miles away from the capital of the state of Wu. When King Wu heard the news, he left Jin and returned to Wu, where he fought with the Yue army in the Five Lakes area. Many battles failed, and even the city gate could not be defended. So the Vietnamese army surrounded the palace and killed King Wu Fucha and his minister. Three years after the destruction of the Wu State, the Yue State dominated the east. Therefore, Zigong's trip saved the state of Lu, disrupted the state of Qi, destroyed the state of Wu, made the state of Jin strong, and enabled the state of Yue to dominate. Zigong's mission caused corresponding changes in the situation of various countries. Within ten years, the situations of Qi, Lu, Wu, Jin, and Yue each changed. Zigong was good at hoarding rare things, buying at low prices and selling at high prices, and changing hands to make profits according to the supply and demand situation.

source: He likes to promote the strengths of others and does not hide the faults of others. He once served as the prime minister of Lu and Wei, and his family fortune accumulated thousands of gold. He eventually died in Qi. Yan Yan was from the state of Wu and his courtesy name was Ziyou. Forty-five years younger than Confucius. After Ziyou received his profession, he served as the governor of Wucheng. Confucius passed by Wucheng and heard the sound of playing the harp and singing. Confucius smiled slightly and said: Why use a knife to kill a chicken? Ziyou: Once upon a time, I heard my husband say: Talented people who learn rituals and music will cultivate their benevolence and love the people; ordinary people who learn rituals and music will abide by laws and regulations and be easy to control. Confucius said to the accompanying students: Everyone, what Yan Yan said is correct. What I just said was just a joke. Confucius believed that Ziyou was familiar with articles and erudite. Bu Shang, courtesy name Zixia. Forty-four years younger than Confucius. Zixia asked: "The beautiful smile is charming and moving, the bright eyes are flowing and shining, and the pure white hair of the Buddha is dyed with brilliant literary colors. What do these three sentences mean?" Confucius replied: Painting must first have a pure white background, and then decorate the picture with color. Zixia said: Did the emergence of ritual and music come after benevolence and righteousness? Confucius said: Fortune teller, now I can discuss the Book of Songs with you. Zigong asked: Which one is stronger, master Zhuan Sun or the diviner? Confucius said: Master, it's a little too much, Shang, it's a little behind. Zigong said: Is Master Zhuan Sun any better? Confucius said: Excess and failure to catch up are equally imperfect. Confucius said to Zixia: You must aspire to be a talented and virtuous scholar, not a shallow and dishonest scholar. After the death of Confucius, Zixia settled in Hexi to teach students and became the teacher of Wei Wenhou. Zixia's son died, and he cried his eyes out. Master Zhuan Sun was a native of Chen State, his courtesy name was Zizhang. Forty-eight years younger than Confucius. Zizhang learned from Confucius how to obtain official salary. Confucius said: Listen more to what others say, and do not make rash comments about unsolved problems. Others should be cautious when speaking out, so that you can make fewer mistakes; watch more people's actions, and don't act rashly about unsolved problems. Others should act cautiously, which can reduce regrets. The fewer mistakes you make in your words and the fewer regrets in your actions, the official salary you seek will be contained in it. One day Zizhang followed Confucius and was besieged between the states of Chen and Cai. Zizhang asked how to make everything work. Confucius said: If you are honest and trustworthy in your words and sincere and respectful in your actions, it will work even in the southern barbarians and Beidi; if you are not loyal and trustworthy in your words and sincere and respectful in your actions, will it work even in your own hometown? When standing, the words "loyalty, trust and reverence" appear before your eyes; when sitting in the car, the words "loyalty, trust and reverence" are hung on the crossbar in front of the car. Once you reach this point, it will work everywhere. Zizhang wrote these words on the big belt around his waist. Zizhang asked: What can a scholar do to be called enlightened? Confucius said: What do you mean by mastery? Zizhang replied: "You must have a good reputation among the princes' states, and you must also have a good reputation in the families of ministers and officials." Confucius said: This is reputation, not understanding. The so-called understanding should be upright and righteous, consider other people's words, observe other people's expressions, and always think about humility and concession. In this way, you will be able to gain access in the states of princes and the fiefdoms of ministers and officials.

He was flawless in acquiring, giving, abandoning, and pursuing, and his reputation spread to the princes in all directions. Confucius heard these things and said: If I judge people by words only, my judgment of Jaeyu is wrong; if I judge people by appearance alone, my judgment of Ziyu is wrong. The words are not neat and the characters are cheap. Thirty years younger than Confucius. Confucius talked about Mi Zi Jian and said: Zi Jian is really a gentleman! If there are no gentlemen in the state of Lu, where did this person learn such good character? Zi Jian was appointed as Shanfu's local governor. He came back and reported to Confucius, saying: "There are five people in this place who are more talented than me. They taught me how to govern the people." Confucius said: What a pity! The areas that are not managed uniformly are too small. If the areas that are managed are large, it will be almost the same. Yuan Xian, courtesy name Zisi. Zisi asked what shame was. Confucius said: If the country's politics are clear, you can be an official and receive a salary, but you can't see trees. The country's politics are dark, and it is a shame to be an official and receive a salary but not be able to stand alone. Zisi said: If competitiveness, self-praising, resentment, and greed are not revealed, can it be regarded as benevolence? Confucius said: It can be said to be commendable. source: The king of Nanyue, Wei Tuo, was from Zhending and his surname was Zhao. The Qin State annexed the six countries, captured and pacified Yang Yue, established Guilin, Nanhai and Xiangjun, and resettled the people who had committed crimes and migrated to these places, and lived together with the Yue people for thirteen years. Wei Tuo was appointed as the magistrate of Longchuan County in Nanhai County during the Qin Dynasty. During the second year of Qin Dynasty, Ren Xiao, the captain of Nanhai County, fell ill and was about to die. He summoned Zhao Tuo, the commander of Longchuan, and said to him: I heard that Chen Sheng and others had launched a rebellion, and that the Qin Dynasty was pursuing cruel and unjust policies, and the people of the world were resentful of this. Xiang Yu, Liu Bang, Chen Sheng, Wu Guang, etc. all gathered people in their respective states and counties at the same time, formed armies, and fought for the world like tigers. The Central Plains region was in turmoil, and it was unknown when peace would be restored. Heroes betrayed the Qin Dynasty and opposed each other. Nanhai County is remote and remote, and I am afraid that the bandit army will invade the land. When I attack here, I want to mobilize the army to cut off the newly built road to the Central Plains. I have taken precautions in advance and wait for the changes in the princes. It happens that I am seriously ill. Let’s talk about Panyu. There are dangerous mountains behind us to rely on, and there is the sea as a barrier to the south. It is thousands of miles away from east to west. We have some Central Plains people to assist us. We can also be the lord of a state and establish a country. There is no one among the governors of Nanhai County who is worthy of me to study these things with him, so I have summoned you to tell you these things. Ren Xiao immediately issued an appointment document to Zhao Tuo, asking him to act on behalf of Nanhai County. After Ren Xiao died, Zhao Tuo sent a message to Hengpu, Yangshan, and Huangxiguan, saying: The bandit army is coming, so we must quickly cut off the road, gather the army, and defend ourselves. Zhao Tuo took this opportunity to gradually use the law to kill the officials installed by the Qin Dynasty, and use his cronies as acting governors. After the Qin Dynasty was destroyed, Zhao Tuo attacked and annexed Guilin and Xiangjun, and established himself as King Wu of South Vietnam. Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty had already pacified the world. Because the people in the Central Plains were tired and miserable, Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty spared Zhao Tuo and did not kill him. source: Mengchangjun's surname is Tian Mingwen. Tian Wen's father is Jingguo Jun Tian Ying. Tian Ying is the youngest son of King Qi Wei and the younger brother of King Qi Xuan's concubine. Tian Ying has been in power since he was King Wei. He once led troops with Chenghou Zou Ji and Tian Ji to rescue South Korea and attack Wei. Later, Chenghou and Tian Ji competed for the favor of King Qi and had a deep rift. As a result, Chenghou betrayed Tian Ji. Tian Ji was very frightened, so he launched a surprise attack on the city on the border of Qi. He failed to capture it and ran away. At this time, King Wei of Qi passed away and King Xuan came to the throne. King Xuan knew that it was Chenghou who framed Tian Ji, so he recalled Tian Ji and made him a general. In the second year of King Xuan of Qi, Tian Ji, Sun Bin and Tian Ying attacked the state of Wei, defeated the state of Wei in Maling, captured the prince Shen of the state of Wei, and killed the general Pang Juan of the state of Wei. In the seventh year of King Xuan, Tian Ying was ordered to go to South Korea and Wei as an envoy. After some of his activities, South Korea and Wei were surrendered to Qi. Tian Ying accompanied Han Zhaohou and King Wei Hui to meet with King Qi Xuan in Dong'anan. The three countries formed an alliance and signed a treaty before leaving. The next year, King Xuan met with King Hui of Liang again in Zhendi. This year, King Hui of Liang passed away. In the ninth year of King Xuan's reign, Tian Ying became prime minister of Qi. King Xuan of Qi and King Xiang of Wei respected each other as kings at the Xuzhou League. After King Chu Wei learned about this incident, he was very angry with Tian Ying and thought that he was the one who planned it. The next year, Chu attacked Qi and defeated the Qi army in Xuzhou, so they sent people to hunt down Tian Ying. Tian Ying sent Zhang Chou to persuade King Chu Wei, and King Chu Wei finally gave up. Tian Ying served as prime minister of Qi for eleven years. King Xuan died and King Min came to the throne. Three years after King Min came to the throne, he granted Tian Ying the title of "Xue Yi". At first, Tian Ying had more than forty sons. One of his concubines gave birth to a son named Wen. Tian Wen was born on May 5th. Tian Ying told Tian Wen's mother: Don't raise him. But Tian Wen's mother still secretly raised him. When he grew up, his mother introduced Tian Wen to Tian Ying through Tian Wen's brother. When Tian Ying saw the child, he angrily said to his mother: I asked you to throw this child away, but you dared to feed him. Why? Before Tian Wen's mother could answer, Tian Wen immediately kowtowed and then asked Tian Ying: "Why are you not allowed to raise a child born in May?" Tian Ying replied: A child born in May will be disadvantageous to his parents when he grows to be as tall as the door. Tian Wen said: Is human destiny granted by God? Or is it awarded by the portal? Tian Ying didn't know how to answer, so he remained silent. Tian Wen continued: If it is granted by God, why should you worry? If it is granted by the portal, then as long as the portal is raised, who can grow so tall! Tian Ying was speechless and scolded: "Stop talking!" After a long time, Tian Wen took the opportunity to ask his father: "What is the name of your son's son?" Tian Ying replied: "Call me grandson." Tian Wen then asked: What is the name of your grandson’s grandson? Tian Ying replied: "My name is Great-grandson." Tian Wen asked again: What is the name of your great-great-grandson's grandson? Tian Ying said: I don’t know anymore. Tian Wen said: You have held great power and served as the prime minister of Qi. You have been kings for three generations. However, the territory of Qi has not expanded, but your private family has accumulated tens of thousands of gold, and there is not a single virtuous person under your family.

He had over forty sons, but Tian Wen was born on May 5th, a date considered inauspicious. Tian Ying ordered the child abandoned, but his mother secretly raised him. When Tian Wen grew up, he confronted his father, arguing that fate was determined by heaven, not by the doorframe, and criticized Tian Ying for accumulating wealth while neglecting the state's welfare. Impressed, Tian Ying made Tian Wen his heir.

I'm secretly weird. From then on, Tian Ying changed his attitude towards Tian Wen, valued him, and asked him to take charge of housekeeping and receive guests. The number of guests kept coming and going, and Tian Wen's reputation spread to all the vassal states. All the vassal states sent people to ask Tian Ying to make Tian Wen the crown prince, and Tian Ying agreed. After Tian Ying's death, he was given the posthumous title of Jing Guojun. As expected, Tian Wen inherited Tian Ying's title in Xue Yi. This is Lord Mengchang. Lord Mengchang was in Xue Yi, soliciting guests from various vassal states and people who had committed crimes and fled. Many people joined Lord Mengchang. Lord Mengchang was willing to give up his family fortune and give them generous treatment, so scholars from all over the world came here to admire his reputation. He has thousands of diners, and all are treated the same as Tian Wen, regardless of high or low. Whenever Mr. Mengchang receives guests and sits and talks with them, he always arranges an attendant behind the screen to record the conversation between Mr. Mengchang and the guests, as well as the residence of the guests' relatives. As soon as the guests left, Lord Mengchang sent envoys to the homes of the guests' relatives to comfort them and offer them gifts. Once, Meng Changjun entertained guests for dinner, and someone blocked the light. The guest was very annoyed, thinking that the quality of the food must be unequal, so he put down his bowls and chopsticks and was about to say goodbye. Lord Mengchang immediately stood up and compared his own food with his. The guest was so ashamed that he cut his neck and committed suicide as an apology. Therefore, many of the wise men were willing to join Lord Mengchang. Mr. Mengchang warmly accepted all the guests who came to his door, without being picky or familiar, and gave them all generous treatment. Therefore, everyone among the guests thought that Lord Mengchang was close to them. When King Zhao of Qin heard that Lord Mengchang was a virtuous man, he first sent Lord Jingyang to Qi as a hostage and asked to see Lord Mengchang. Lord Mengchang was about to go to Qin, but the guests did not approve of his trip and tried to persuade him, but he refused to listen and insisted on going. At this time, a guest, Su Dai, said to him: I came out this morning and saw a puppet man and a clay puppet talking. The puppet man said: As soon as it rains, you will collapse. The earth puppet said: I was born from the earth. Even if it collapses, I will return to the earth. If it really rains and the water rushes towards you, I don’t know where it will take you. Today's Qin State is a country as fierce as a tiger or a wolf. If you insist on going there, if you cannot come back, will you not be laughed at by the local puppets? After hearing this, Lord Mengchang realized the truth and stopped preparing for the trip. In the twenty-fifth year of King Min of Qi, he finally sent Lord Mengchang to Qin. source: Someone among the officials persuaded the King of Qin: Lord Mengchang is indeed a virtuous man, but he is a member of the Qi clan and now serves as the prime minister of the Qin State. When planning things, he must first plan for the Qi State and then consider the interests of the Qin State. This will put the Qin State in danger. So King Zhao of Qin dismissed Lord Mengchang from his position as prime minister. He imprisoned Lord Mengchang and wanted to kill Lord Mengchang. Lord Mengchang knew that the situation was critical, so he sent someone to see King Zhao's concubine to ask for help. The concubine made a condition and said: I hope to get Lord Mengchang's white fox fur. When Lord Mengchang came, he brought with him a white fox fur, which was worth thousands of gold. There was no second one in the world. When he arrived in Qin, he presented it to King Zhao, and there was no other fur. Lord Mengchang was worried about this matter. He asked all the guests, but no one could think of a solution. There was a man who was not very capable but could steal things in dog skins. He said: I can get that white fox fur. So that night, he disguised himself as a dog, went into the warehouse of the Qin Palace, took out the fox white fur that was presented to King Zhao, and took it back and presented it to King Zhao's concubine. After getting the concubine, she interceded with King Zhao on behalf of Lord Mengchang, and King Zhao released Lord Mengchang. After Mengchangjun was released, he immediately fled by express train, changed his exit certificate, changed his name and escaped from the city pass. We arrived at Hangu Pass at midnight. King Zhao regretted releasing Lord Mengchang and sent people to look for him again. When he found that he had escaped, he immediately sent people to chase him. Mengchangjun and his party arrived at Hangu Pass. According to the customs law, guests can only be let out when the rooster crows. Mengchangjun was worried that his pursuers would arrive. Among the guests, there was a person who was of low rank but could imitate the rooster's crow. As soon as he imitated the rooster's crow, the nearby chickens also crowed, and he immediately showed his documents and escaped from Hangu Pass. After about a meal after leaving the pass, Qin's pursuers arrived at Hangu Pass, but fell behind Lord Mengchang, so they had to go back. When Lord Mengchang accepted these two people as guests, the guests all felt ashamed and disgraced. When Lord Mengchang suffered a disaster in Qin, he finally relied on these two people to escape. From then on, the guests all admired Mengchangjun's approach of recruiting guests regardless of their status. Lord Mengchang passed by the State of Zhao, and Lord Pingyuan of the State of Zhao treated him as a distinguished guest. When the people of Zhao heard about Mengchang's talents, they all came out to watch and see him. When they saw him, they all laughed and said: "I thought Mengchang was a tall man, but now I see him, he is just a skinny man." Mengchangjun was very angry after hearing these teasing words. The guests who were traveling with him jumped out of the car, killed hundreds of people, and left after destroying a county. King Qi Min felt guilty for sending Lord Mengchang to Qin. After Lord Mengchang returned to Qi State, the King of Qi made him prime minister of Qi State and in charge of state affairs. Lord Mengchang resented Qin and planned to unite South Korea and Wei to attack Qin on the grounds that Qi had helped South Korea and Wei attack Chu. To this end, he borrowed weapons and rations from the Western Zhou Dynasty.

source: On behalf of the Western Zhou Dynasty, Su said to Lord Mengchang: You used the troops of Qi to help Han and Wei attack Chu for nine years, and gained the area north of Wan and Ye. As a result, Han and Wei became stronger. Now if you attack Qin, it will further strengthen the power of Han and Wei. If South Korea and Wei have no worries from Chu in the south, and no troubles from Qin in the north, then Qi will be in danger. When Korea and Wei become stronger, they will despise Qi and fear Qin. I really feel uneasy about this situation for you. It is better for you to let the Western Zhou Dynasty have a deep friendship with Qin State. You should not attack Qin State and do not borrow weapons and food. You send your army to Hangu Pass but do not attack. Let the Western Zhou Dynasty tell King Zhao of Qin your feelings and say that Duke Xue will definitely not attack Qin to strengthen the power of Han and Wei. His purpose in attacking Qin was just to ask the king to instruct Chu to cede the Eastern Kingdom to Qi, and to ask you to release King Huai of Chu to reach a reconciliation. You asked the Western Zhou Dynasty to use this method to benefit Qin. Qin could not be attacked and used Chu's territory to protect itself. Qin must want to do this. If the King of Chu could be released, he would definitely be grateful to the State of Qi. The Qi State will naturally become stronger and stronger after acquiring the Dong Kingdom, and Xue Yi will be free from worries for generations. Qin will not be overly weakened, and it is located to the west of South Korea and Wei. South Korea and Wei must rely on Qi. After hearing this, Lord Mengchang immediately said: "Okay." So Han and Wei were asked to congratulate Qin, which prevented a military disaster. Qi, Han, and Wei no longer sent troops to attack, and Qi stopped borrowing weapons and rations from the Western Zhou Dynasty. At this time, King Huai of Chu had already arrived in Qin, and Qin detained him, so Lord Mengchang must ask Qin to release him. But Qin did not do this. When Mengchang Jun was the prime minister of Qi, his attendant Wei Zi went to collect the tax from the feudal city for him. He made three trips back and forth, but he never got the tax back once. Lord Mengchang asked him what was the reason for this, and Wei Zi replied: There is a virtuous man. I donated the tax to him privately in your name, so I did not take it back. After hearing this, Lord Mengchang became angry and dismissed Wei Zi. A few years later, someone spread rumors about Lord Mengchang to King Min of Qi, saying that Lord Mengchang was about to launch a rebellion. When Tian Junjia kidnapped King Min, King Min suspected that it was Master Mengchang who planned it, and fled to avoid disaster. The sage who had received food as a gift from Wei Zi heard about this and wrote to King Min to state that Lord Mengchang would not cause rebellion and asked for his own life as a guarantee. He then cut his neck and committed suicide at the gate of the palace to prove Lord Mengchang's innocence. King Min was shocked, so he investigated and inquired about the actual situation. As expected, Lord Mengchang had no rebellion conspiracy, so he recalled Lord Mengchang. Lord Mengchang therefore excused himself from illness and asked to resign and return to Xue Yi to retire. King Min agreed to his request. After that, Qin's fugitive general Lu Li came to Qi to serve as Qi's prime minister. He wanted to put Su Dai in trouble. Su Dai said to Lord Mengchang: Zhou Zui was extremely loyal to the King of Qi, but the King of Qi expelled him and listened to the advice of his relatives and made Lu Li the prime minister. The reason was that he planned to unite with Qin.

source: When Lord Mengchang heard that Feng Chen had burned the deed, he was very angry and immediately sent someone to recall Feng Chen. As soon as Feng Chen arrived, Lord Mengchang asked: "I have three thousand diners, so I lend money in Xue Yi." My fiefdom is small to begin with, but the people still do not repay the interest on time, and the guests are afraid that they will not have enough to eat, so I asked you, sir, to collect the debts. I heard that after receiving the money, my husband held a banquet of wine and meat and burned the deed. Why is this? Feng Xuan replied: Yes. If there is no way to gather all the debtors together without throwing a feast of wine and meat, there will be no way to know who is rich and who is poor. If he is wealthy, he will be given a set date to repay his debts. The poor will not be able to repay their debts even if they are detained for ten years. The longer the time, the higher the interest. If you are too hasty, they will not be able to repay you in the end. On the one hand, you will be thought to be greedy for small profits and not caring for the people. On the other hand, the people will have a reputation of abandoning the emperor and relying on debts. This is not a way to encourage scholars and people and show your reputation. I burned the useless IOUs and discarded the nominal account books to make the common people of Xue Yi trust you and promote your good reputation for kindness. What else do you have to doubt? After hearing this, Lord Mengchang clapped his hands and thanked him repeatedly. The King of Qi was bewitched by the slanderous remarks of Qin and Chu, and believed that Lord Mengchang's reputation was higher than his own and that he would monopolize the power of Qi, so he dismissed Lord Mengchang from his official position. When the guests saw that Lord Mengchang had been dismissed, they all left him. Only Feng Xuan planned for him and said: Lend me a car and let me go to Qin. I will definitely make you more prominent in Qi and your city will be wider. Do you think it's okay? So Mengchangjun prepared a carriage and gifts to send Feng Xuan on the road. Feng Chen then drove west to the state of Qin to lobby the king of Qin, saying: All lobbyists in the world who drive west to the state of Qin all want to make Qin strong and make Qi weak; everyone who rides east to enter the state of Qi all want to make Qi strong and make Qin weak. These are two countries with no distinction between superior and inferior. It is impossible for them to stand side by side and dominate. The one who dominates can unify the world. The King of Qin was fascinated by what he heard. He straightened up and knelt down and asked Feng Xuan: "What do you think should be done to prevent Qin from becoming a weak country?" Feng Chen replied: Your Majesty also knows that the State of Qi has dismissed Lord Mengchang from his position, right? King Qin said: I heard about this. Feng Xuan said: The person who made Qi respected by the world was Lord Mengchang. Now that the king of Qi has listened to the slander and dismissed Lord Mengchang, Lord Mengchang is extremely resentful and will definitely betray Qi. If he betrays Qi and enters Qin, then the national conditions of Qi and the situation in the court, from the king to the officials, will be under the control of Qin. You will get the entire land of Qi, and you will be more than just the hero! Hurry up and send an envoy with gifts to meet Lord Mengchang secretly. Don't miss this opportunity. If King Qi comes to his senses and appoints Lord Mengchang again, then it is impossible to predict who will win or lose. The King of Qin was very happy after hearing this, and sent ten carriages carrying a hundred yi gold to meet Lord Mengchang. Feng Xuan said goodbye to the King of Qin and rushed to the State of Qi ahead of the envoy. When he arrived at the State of Qi, he persuaded the King of Qi: The lobbyists from all over the world who drive east to Qi State all want to make Qi strong and make Qin weak; those who ride west to Qin State all want to make Qin strong and make Qi weak. Qin and Qi are equally superior and inferior. If Qin is strong, Qi must be weak. These two countries will inevitably not be able to dominate at the same time. Now I heard privately that the Qin State has sent an envoy with ten carriages carrying a hundred yi gold to greet Lord Mengchang. It's fine if Lord Mengchang doesn't go west. If he goes west and serves as the prime minister of Qin, then the world will belong to Qin. If Qin becomes the lord, Qi will have no choice but to succumb to it. Then Linzi and Jimo will be in danger. Why didn't the king quickly restore Mengchang to his official position and increase his fiefdom to apologize to him before the Qin envoy arrived? If this is done, Lord Mengchang will be happy and willing to accept it. Although Qin is a powerful country, how can it arbitrarily go to other countries to welcome other people's prime ministers? It is necessary to thwart Qin's conspiracy and cut off its plan to seek strength and hegemony. After hearing this, King Qi immediately understood and said: OK. So he sent people to the border to wait for the Qin envoy. As soon as the Qin envoy's car entered the Qi border, the Qi envoy at the border immediately changed his car and drove back to report the situation. The King of Qi recalled Mengchang Jun and restored his position as prime minister. At the same time, he also gave him the land of the original fiefdom and added a thousand households to him. When the envoy from Qin heard that Lord Mengchang had restored his position as prime minister of Qi, he changed his carriage and went back. Since the King of Qi dismissed Lord Mengchang because of the slander, all the guests have left him. Later, the King of Qi recalled and restored Lord Mengchang to his official position, and Feng Chen went to greet him.

When King Wei of Qi was in power, he liked to talk in argot, feast all night long, indulge in excessive drinking, ignored state affairs, and entrusted political affairs to the officials. None of the ministers around King Qi dared to give advice. Chunyu Kun used argot to admonish and admonish King Wei of Qi, saying: There is a big bird in the capital that landed in the king's courtyard. It has not flown or screamed for three years. Does the king know what happened to this bird? King Wei of Qi said: If this bird does not fly, it will go straight to the sky; if it does not scream, it will amaze people. So he ordered all the chiefs of the seventy-two counties in the country to come to the court to report. They rewarded one person and killed another. They also sent troops to defend against the enemy. The princes and states were shocked and returned the occupied land to Qi. Qi's prestige lasted for thirty-six years. All these things are recorded in "Tian Wan Family". In the eighth year of King Wei of Qi's reign, the State of Chu sent a large army to invade its borders. The King of Qi sent Chunyu Kun as an envoy to the State of Zhao to request reinforcements, and asked him to carry a gift of a hundred catties of gold and ten four-horse carriages. Chunyu Kun looked up to the sky and laughed so hard that the string holding his hat broke. King Wei said: Sir, do you think the gift is too little? Chunyu Kun said: How dare you think too little! King Wei said: Then you laugh, do you have any excuse? Chunyu Kun said: Today I came from the east and saw a man worshiping the God of the Fields by the roadside. He held a pig's trotter and a glass of wine and prayed: "The grain harvested in the highlands fills the bonnet, and the crops harvested in the low fields fill the vehicles; the grains are lush and ripe, and the rice grains are piled up in the warehouse." I saw that he brought few sacrifices and prayed for many things, so I laughed at him. source: Li Shiqi was from Gaoyang, Chenliu. He likes to study very much, but his family is poor and destitute. He doesn't even have a property that can afford to clothe and feed himself, so he has to work as a lowly clerk looking after the inner door. But despite this, the wise men and powerful men in the county did not dare to use him casually. People in the county called him "Kangsheng". When Chen Sheng, Xiang Liang and others rebelled against the Qin Dynasty, dozens of generals passed through Gaoyang when they attacked the city. However, Li Shiqi heard that these people were narrow-minded, liked trivial etiquette, were self-willed, and could not listen to open-minded words. So he lived in seclusion and hid himself, not to cater to these people. Later, he heard that Pei Gong led troops to capture the city and came to the outskirts of Chenliu. One of Pei Gong's cavalrymen happened to be the son of an old friend of Li Shi's neighborhood. Pei Gong often asked him about the wise men and heroes in his hometown. One day, when the cavalry came home, Li Shiqi saw him and said to him: I heard that Pei Gong was arrogant and looked down upon others, but he had many far-reaching strategies. This is the person I really want to follow, but I have no one to introduce him to him. When you see Pei Gong, you can say this to him: There is a Mr. Li in my hometown who is over sixty years old and eight feet tall. People call him a crazy person, but he himself says that he is not a crazy person. The cavalryman replied: Pei Gong does not like Confucian scholars. Many people came to see him wearing Confucian scholar hats. He immediately took off their hats and urinated in them. When he talked to people, he often cursed. So you'd better not lobby him as a Confucian scholar. Li Shiqi said: Just say it like I taught you. After the knight returned, he told Pei Gong according to Li Sheng's instructions. Later, Pei Gong came to Gaoyang, stayed in an inn, and sent someone to summon Li Shiqi to come and see him. When Li Sheng came to the hotel, Pei Gong sat on the bed with his legs spread apart and asked two women to wash his feet. He called Li Sheng to see him. Li Sheng went in, only made a long salute without leaning down to worship, and said: "Do you want to help Qin attack the princes, or do you want to lead the princes to destroy Qin?" Pei Gong scolded: You Confucian scholar! The people of the world have been suffering from the Qin Dynasty for a long time, so the princes have raised armies to resist the violent Qin one after another. How can you help the Qin Dynasty attack the princes? Li Sheng said: If you are determined to gather the people and call for volunteers to overthrow the tyrannical and cruel Qin Dynasty, you should not receive the elders in such a arrogant and disrespectful manner. So Pei Gong immediately stopped washing his feet, tidied his clothes, invited Li Sheng to the guest's seat, and apologized to him. Li Sheng talked about the strategy used by the six kingdoms to unite vertically and horizontally. Pei Gong was very happy and ordered people to bring rice for Li Sheng to eat. Then he asked: "Then how do you think we should formulate our strategy today?" Li Sheng said: If you gather the rabble and scattered soldiers, the total is less than 10,000 people. If you use this to directly confront the powerful Qin, it will be what people often say is exploring the tiger's mouth. Chenliu is an important transportation thoroughfare in the world, extending in all directions. Now there is a lot of grain in the city. I am very close to the magistrate of Chenliu. Please send me to him to ask him to surrender to you. If he doesn't obey, you can send troops to attack the city again, and I can act as an internal response in the city. He followed Emperor Gaozu to pacify the world as a guest of staff. People at that time called him a very eloquent lobbyist, so he accompanied Emperor Gaozu and often traveled to various vassal states as envoys. When Emperor Gaozu had just pacified the Central Plains, Wei Ta also pacified South Vietnam and established himself as king there. Emperor Gaozu considered that the world had been settled for the first time, so he did not execute Wei Ta. He also sent Lu Jia with the seal of the King of South Vietnam given to Wei Ta to appoint him. When Lu Sheng arrived in South Vietnam, he wore his hair in an awl-like bun popular in the area, sat with his legs spread like a dustpan, and met Lu Sheng. Lu Sheng said to Wei Ta: You are from the Central Plains, and the graves of your relatives, brothers and ancestors are all in Zhending. But now that you have gone against the customs of the Central Plains people, abandoned your clothes and scarves, and want to use Xiaonan, who has only a small place, to compete with the emperor and become an enemy country, then your disaster will be imminent. Moreover, the Qin Dynasty was tyrannical and ruthless, and all the princes and heroes rose up one after another. Only the King of Han entered the pass first and occupied Xianyang. Xiang Yu betrayed the alliance and established himself as the overlord of Western Chu. The princes all belonged to him, and he could be said to be extremely powerful. This is not something that humans can do, but is the result of God’s help. Now the Emperor of the Han Dynasty has heard that you are proclaimed king in South Vietnam and is unwilling to help the people of the world to quell the rebellion. The generals and ministers of the Han Dynasty want to lead their troops to destroy you. source: Wei Bao was originally the son of the Wei Kingdom during the Six Kingdoms period. His elder brother is Wei Jiu, who was named Lord Ningling when he was in Wei State. After the Qin State destroyed the Wei State, he was exiled to other places and became a commoner. Chen Sheng rebelled and proclaimed himself king, and Wei Jiu followed him. King Chen sent Zhou Shi, a native of Wei, to lead troops to seize the land of Wei. After Wei was captured, everyone discussed with each other and wanted to make Zhou Shi the king of Wei. After five trips in total, King Chen agreed to send Wei Jiu back and establish him as King of Wei. Not long after Zhang Han defeated King Chen, he marched to Linji to attack King Wei. King Wei sent Zhou Shi to Qi and Chu to request reinforcements. Qi and Chu sent Xiang Ta and Tian Ba ​​to lead the army to follow Zhou City to rescue Wei. Zhang Han actually defeated the reinforcements, killed Zhou Shi, and surrounded Linji. Wei Jiu proposed conditions for surrender for the sake of the soldiers and people in the city. After the negotiation was successful, Wei Jiu set himself on fire and died. Wei Bao fled to Chu. King Huai of Chu gave Wei Bao thousands of troops and went back to capture Wei. He planned to occupy the Liang land, so he moved King Bao of Wei to Hedong, established his capital in Pingyang, and named him King of the Western Wei Dynasty. Wei Bao surrendered the entire country to the King of Han and followed the King of Han to Pengcheng to attack the Chu army. The king of Han was defeated and returned to Xingyang. Wei Bao asked for leave and went home to visit his mother's condition. After returning home, he immediately cut off the crossing of the Yellow River and betrayed the King of Han. Although the King of Han heard the news of Wei Bao's rebellion, he was worried about the Chu State in the east. He had no time to attack him, so he said to Li Sheng: Go and persuade Wei Bao for me. If you can persuade him, I will make you the Marquis of Wanhu. Li Sheng went to lobby Wei Bao. Wei Bao politely refused and said: Life is as short as the shadow of the sun passing through the crack in the wall. Now the King of Han is arrogant and insults others at will. He scolds the princes and ministers as if they were slaves. He has no etiquette at all. I can't bear to see him. So the King of Han sent Han Xin to attack Wei Bao, captured Wei Bao in Hedong, and escorted him to Xingyang in a post car, and changed Wei Bao's original territory into three counties. The King of Han ordered Wei Bao to garrison Xingyang. When the Chu army tightened its siege, Zhou Ke killed Wei Bao. Peng Yue was from Changyi, with the courtesy name Zhong. He often fishes in Juye Lake and joins a group of people to commit robberies. source: Peng Yue said: Now is the time for the two dragons to fight, so let's wait. More than a year later, more than a hundred young people from Zezhong gathered to follow Peng Yue and said, "Please be our leader." Peng Yue refused and said: I don't want to work with you. The young people persisted in their request, and he agreed. Make an appointment with them to gather when the sun rises the next day, and those who are late will be beheaded. When the sun came up the next day, more than ten people were late, and the last one didn't come until noon. At that time, Peng Yue said apologetically: I am old and you insist on making me the leader. I just don't dare to be late again from now on." So Peng Yue took the last person who arrived and killed him. Set up an earthen altar, use human heads to offer sacrifices, and give orders to everyone who belongs to them. Everyone was shocked and afraid of Peng Yue. No one dared to look up at him. So he led everyone to seize the land and collected more than a thousand soldiers who had fled from the princes. Peigong went north from Dang to attack Changyi, and Peng Yue assisted him. Changyi was not captured, so Pei Gong led the army to march west. Peng Yue also led his troops to garrison in Juye Ze to collect the fleeing soldiers of Wei. Xiang Ji entered Guanzhong and divided the feudal lords, and then returned. Peng Yue's army had grown to more than 10,000 people, but he had no one to belong to. In the autumn of the first year of Han Dynasty, King Tian Rong of Qi betrayed King Xiang, so he sent someone to give General Peng Yue a seal and asked him to march to Jiyin to attack the Chu army. The Chu army ordered Xiao Gongjiao to lead his troops to attack Peng Yue, but was severely defeated by Peng Yue. In the spring of the second year of the Han Dynasty, the King of Han, King Bao of Wei and various princes went east to attack Chu. Peng Yue led more than 30,000 troops to join the King of Han in Waihuang. The King of Han said: General Peng has recovered more than a dozen cities in Wei and is eager to support the descendants of King Wei. Today, King Bao of Wei is the cousin of King Jiu of Wei and a descendant of the real King of Wei. He appointed Peng Yue as the Prime Minister of Wei State, monopolizing military power and pacifying the Liang Dynasty. After the King of Han was defeated in Pengcheng, he retreated westward. At this time, Peng Yue abandoned all the cities he had captured and led his army alone to the north to station along the Yellow River. In the third year of the Han Dynasty, Peng Yue often traveled and sent troops on behalf of the Han Dynasty, attacked the Chu army, and cut off their supply of food and grass in Liang. In the winter of the fourth year of the Han Dynasty, King Xiang and King Han were at a stalemate in Xingyang, and Peng Yue captured seventeen cities including Suiyang and Waihuang. When King Xiang heard the news, he sent Cao Jiu to garrison Chenggao, and he led his army eastward to recover the cities that Pengyue had conquered, returning them to Chu. Peng Yue led his team north to Gucheng. In the autumn of the fifth year of the Han Dynasty, King Xiang's army retreated south to Xia Yang. Peng Yue captured more than 20 cities near Changyi and seized more than 100,000 bushels of grain, which was used as ration for the King of Han. The king of Han was defeated and sent an envoy to ask Peng Yue to join forces to attack the Chu army. Peng Yue said: Wei has just been pacified, but it is still afraid of the Chu army and cannot go there. The king of Han raised his troops to pursue the Chu army, but was defeated by Xiang Ji in Guling.

He used Ding Jinlin to lead the soldiers to cross the river first, send a message to the prefecture and the country, attack the camp and seize the territory, and captured 21 counties in Henan, Chenliu and Sichuan. All the generals occupied Fengyi Mei County, but Ding Linlin was the only one willing to grant the title to his hometown. Someone said to Ding Jinlin: Everyone wants to occupy the county, but you only want the hometown. Why is this? Ding Jinlin said: In the past, Sun Shuao told his son that when he was granted a title, he must seek a barren land. Now that I can do a small job, it will be great to get a rural pavilion. The emperor obeyed and named him Marquis of Xin'an Township, Dingling, with a settlement of 5,000 households. Later, he was renamed Marquis of Lingyang. When Ding Hongnian was 13 years old, he studied "Ouyang Shangshu" from Huan Rong. In three years, he understood the chapters and sentences, could debate and speak for everyone, so he determined to further his studies, put on civilian clothes, carried his luggage, and traveled thousands of miles to study. At first, Ding Jinlin followed Shizu in the expedition, and Ding Hong lived with his younger brother Ding Sheng. They loved Ding Sheng when he was young and lived a poor life together. After Ding Jinlin's death, Ding Hong was granted the hereditary title and wrote a letter to transfer the country to Ding Sheng, but received no reply. His father had been buried, so he hung mourning clothes in the tomb and slipped away, leaving a message to Ding Sheng: "Hong was greedy for scriptures. He ignored his kindness and righteousness. He studied with his teacher when he was young. He did not support his parents during his life. He could not fulfill his filial piety until his death. The ancestors of the emperor and heaven did not bless and help him. He was seriously ill and could not bear the soil." The last time I wrote a letter stating my illness, I was willing to resign my title to my younger brother, but the memorial was shelved without a reply, and the time was approaching for me to be granted a title. I would like to give up the title and seek good doctors abroad. If the disease cannot be cured, forget about dying in a ravine. Ding Hong initially became a student with Huan Rong, a colleague of Bao Jun from Jiujiang, and the two had a close friendship. Later, Ding Hong escaped from the throne and met Bao Jun in the East China Sea. Ding Hong pretended not to know Bao Jun. Bao Jun took Ding Hong's arm and scolded him: "In the past, Boyi and Wu Jizha were in troubled times, so they had to express their ambition to surrender the country." The great righteousness of "Spring and Autumn" is not to waste the king's affairs because of family affairs. Now you are using your brother's affair to cut off your father's immortal inheritance. Bao Jun also wrote a letter saying that Ding Hong was a good scholar and practiced the classics, and Xianzong appreciated him very much. In the 10th year of Yongping, the emperor issued an edict to recruit talents. Ding Hong was summoned when he arrived and told the story of "The Order of Marquis Wen". The emperor bestowed royal robes and ribbons, food and carriage, and received the same courtesy as a doctor.

Ding Hong returned, taught disciples, and was later summoned by Emperor Xianzong, becoming a servant and then Captain of Shesheng. He died in the sixth year of Yongyuan.

source: ◆The biography of Yu Xu, whose courtesy name was Shengqing, was from Wuping in the state of Chen. My grandfather, Yu Jing, was a county prison officer. He handled cases impartially, was generous, and respected himself and others. Every winter month, the case is reported, and I often shed tears over it. He once said: In the East China Sea, a gate was built at the Duke's height, and the horses and chariots were made high, thinking that some of their descendants would become high officials. And his son Dingguo finally became prime minister. I have been in prison for sixty years. Although I am not as good as Yu Gong, maybe it is about the same. My descendants may not become Jiuqing. Therefore, Yu Xu was given the title "Qing". Yu Xu was twelve years old and could read Shangshu. Is an orphan. Take care of your grandmother. The county elected him as his grandson, and the prime minister admired him very much and wanted him to be an official. Yu Xu declined and said: "Grandma is ninety years old. Without me, there is no one to take care of her." The Prime Minister didn't ask him to go. After his grandmother passed away and the period of mourning expired, he was recruited into Taiwei Li's Mansion and was awarded the title of doctor. In the fourth year of Yongchu, the Qiang rebelled and ravaged Bing and Liang. The general Deng Zhi thought that the military situation was tense and could not take care of both. He wanted to abandon Liangzhou and concentrate his forces on the north. So he summoned the ministers for a meeting, and Deng Zhi said: For example, if your clothes are broken, if you repair one broken piece and repair another, one piece will still be intact. If not, there will be no protection. Everyone at the meeting agreed. After hearing this, Yu Xu said to Li: "It is said that Gongqing decided to abandon Liangzhou. In my opinion, it is inappropriate." The late emperor worked hard to open up the territory, but now he was afraid of the trouble and threw it away. Since Liangzhou is lost, then the Third Assistant is regarded as a frontier fortress. If the Third Assistant is a frontier fortress, then the ancestral garden tombs are outside the boundary. This is absolutely unacceptable. As the saying goes: Guanxi produces prime ministers, Guandong produces generals, Liangzhou trains troops and trains bravery, surpassing other states. Now the Qiang and Hu dare not invade Sanfu because Liangzhou is behind him and is his thorn in the side! The people of Liangzhou took up arms to defend Liangzhou without any hesitation, because Liangzhou belonged to the Han Dynasty! If you abandon it and move the people away, and the people are content with their homeland and are unwilling to move, something will happen. Suppose the heroes gather together and take advantage of the situation to come eastward. Even though there are warriors like Ben and Yu and generals like Taigong, they may not be able to withstand it. The speaker used the analogy of mending clothes that has yet to be completed. I see it as a ulcer that gets wider and wider and never stops. Abandoning Liangzhou is not a strategy. Li said: I didn't expect that. It’s not like you said that it almost failed in national affairs. So, what’s a good strategy? Yu Xu said: There is a commotion in Liangzhou today, and people are uneasy. I am worried that something unexpected will happen. The nine ministers of the four prefectures should be ordered to recommend several people from their respective states, and all the eldest sons of the Mu Shou Ling should be given official positions. On the surface, it is to reward their merits, but in fact, it is to monitor them and prevent them from causing trouble. Li thought he was right, and even extended the four prefectures to follow Yu Xu's plan. So he recruited the heroes of the two states as vassals, and appointed the sons of the shepherds and guardians as ministers to comfort them. The Deng Zhi brothers were dissatisfied because Yu Xu opposed Deng Zhi's opinions. He wanted to use the official law to frame Yu Xu.
gold_target: Yu Xu, from Wuping in Chen, was known for his integrity. His grandfather, a prison officer, handled cases with compassion. Yu Xu was orphaned young and cared for his grandmother, refusing an official post until after her death. He later served as a doctor. When General Deng Zhi proposed abandoning Liangzhou due to Qiang rebellions, Yu Xu argued against it, stating it would expose the imperial tombs and that Liangzhou's people were a vital defense. He suggested controlling local leaders by giving their sons official posts to prevent rebellion. Deng Zhi, resentful of Yu Xu's opposition, sent him to govern Chaoge, a bandit-ridden area. Yu Xu used deception, recruiting former bandits to ambush others and marking thieves' clothes with silk threads, leading to their dispersal. Promoted to Wudu's prefect, he again used deception against the Qiang, increasing his campfires to feign strength and marching rapidly. He then used a strategy of weak arrows to lure the Qiang into range of his strong crossbows, defeating them. He improved the county by building fortifications, opening waterways for transport, and increasing the population. As Sili Xiaowei, he impeached powerful officials, earning their hatred. He was framed and sentenced to hard labor, but eunuch Sun Cheng defended him, leading to his release and promotion. He later abolished the practice of "righteous money" and argued for fair treatment of petitioners. He remained upright despite nine reprimands and three punishments, dying as Shangshu Ling. On his deathbed, he regretted killing many bandits at Chaoge, believing it brought divine punishment.

Zhao Zhong was even more resentful, but he was too famous to dare to harm him. There are also many powerful people who are jealous of him, so they are not allowed to stay in the court and become the governor of Hanyang. At first, Fan Jin, the general of the county, had the knack of knowing people and promoted Fu Xie as Xiaolian. Later, Fan Jin was appointed as the prefect of Hanyang. Fan Jin, courtesy name Wenyuan, was from Nanyang. Fu Xie was good at sympathizing with people, and the rebellious Qiang people were moved by his kindness and enlightenment, and they all surrendered. He cleared the land and cultivated fields and set up more than forty camps to accommodate them. At this time, the governor Geng Bi appointed Cheng Qiu to be in charge. Cheng Qiu sought personal gain for him and associated with traitors, and the soldiers hated him. In the fourth year of Zhongping, Geng Bi led soldiers from six counties to conquer the Kingdom of Jincheng, Han Sui and others. Fu Xie knew that Geng Bi had broken people's trust and must fail. The admonishment said: The emperor has not been in power for a long time, and the people do not know how to educate him. Confucius said: To make people fight without first teaching them is to abandon them. Now he leads untrained men across the dangers of Dalong. There will be ten dangers and ten dangers. When the thieves hear that the army is coming, they will surely unite as one. The border soldiers are brave and difficult to resist; the newly organized troops are not harmonious among the officers and soldiers. If internal changes occur, it will be too late to regret it. It is better to let the army rest for a period of time, improve discipline, and strictly enforce rewards and punishments. When the thieves learn that our army is lax, they must think that our army is cowardly, and they will surely fall apart due to their internal struggle for power. Then lead the trained troops to defeat the disintegrating thieves, and then sit back and wait for victory to come. Now if you don't seek to be foolproof and take a path that is bound to fail, I won't do it for you. Geng Bi refused to listen. When the troops arrived at Didao, there were indeed rebels. At this time, thousands of Hu cavalry from the north followed the bandits to attack Hanyang County. They all cherished Fu Xie's kindness for a long time. They kowtowed outside the city and asked to send Fu Xie back to his hometown.
gold_target: Fu Xie, from Lingzhou, was known for his caution in speech and action. He served as Sima under Huangfu Song against Zhang Jiao's Yellow Turbans. Before the campaign, he warned the emperor that the real threat was internal, from eunuchs like Zhao Zhong, and that evil and good cannot coexist. Despite his merits, Zhao Zhong framed him, but the emperor spared him. Later, when Situ Cui Lie proposed abandoning Liangzhou during a Xiqiang rebellion, Fu Xie vehemently opposed him, arguing that Liangzhou was the empire's shield and that abandoning it would empower the barbarians. The emperor agreed. Fu Xie refused to curry favor with the powerful eunuch Zhao Zhong, even when offered a marquisate. As Hanyang's governor, he pacified the Qiang. He warned Governor Geng Bi against attacking Han Sui with untrained troops, predicting disaster. Geng Bi ignored him and was killed. When Hanyang was besieged, Fu Xie refused to abandon the city despite his son's pleas and the offer of safe passage from grateful Hu cavalry. He chose to die in battle, cursing a defecting official. His posthumous title was Zhuangjiehou.

Although Gai Xun was a local official and had military and state secrets, Emperor Ling often issued edicts to ask him. He received many rewards and trusted him very much. source: ◆Yuan Shao Zhuan, Yuan Shao, courtesy name Benchu, was born in Ruyang, Runan, and was the grandson of Situ Yuan Tang. Yuan Shao's father, Yuan Cheng, had served as a lieutenant general with five senses. He was physically strong and liked to make friends. From the time of the great general Liang Ji, he was always friends with him. Yuan Shao served as a Langguan when he was young, and was later appointed as the Chief of Puyang. When his mother died, he resigned from the official position. After serving three years of funeral service, Yuan Shao recalled and lamented that he had lost his father since childhood and had to attend the funeral service for his father. After the mourning period expired, he moved to Luoyang. Yuan Shao was elegant, beautiful, kind to others, and focused on reputation. source: Che Qianqiu is the prime minister, loyal, honest and virtuous. Whenever ministers and ministers met, Huo Guang would say to Che Qianqiu: "Back then, I accepted the Emperor's mission with you. Now that Huo Guang is in charge of internal affairs and you are in charge of foreign affairs, what should I have to enlighten and urge me so that I don't let down the trust of the people of the world?" Che Qianqiu said: General, please pay more attention, it will be the greatest honor in the world. He always refused to express any objection to Huo Guang's dictatorship. Huo Guang therefore valued Che Qianqiu very much. Every time an auspicious occasion appears, he will praise and reward the prime minister with a thousand-year-old car. Until the death of Emperor Zhao, the country had few affairs and the people gradually became rich and fulfilled. In the sixth year of the First Yuan Dynasty, Emperor Zhao Shao ordered the county to recommend virtuous and literary people, and asked them about the sufferings of the people, which led to the discussion of salt and iron. Che Qianqiu served as prime minister for twelve years. After his death, Mi was named Dinghou. At first, when Che Qianqiu was old, the emperor treated him favorably and showed up to the court. He was allowed to enter the palace in a small car, so he was known as the "Prime Minister of Cars". Che Qianqiu's son Tian Shun succeeded him as a marquis and became the prefect of Yunzhong County. At that time, Emperor Xuan was serving as General Huya to attack the Xiongnu. He was convicted of committing suicide for illegally increasing the number of prisoners and taking credit, and the feudal state was cancelled. Sang Hongyang worked as a censor for eight years. He thought it would benefit the country and boasted about his achievements. He wanted to get official positions for the children of the Sang family. He resented Huo Guang and rebelled against Shangguan Jie and others, and was finally executed. Wang Xin is from Jinan County. As a junior official in the county, he accumulated merit and was gradually promoted to the magistrate of Baiyang County. In the last years of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty, the army often went on expeditions, and thieves gathered in the counties and counties. The embroidered censor's sudden victory directed the envoys to hunt down the thieves with axes, and dealt with the property collected by the local officials according to the amount of property collected and handed over to the court for military use. Officials with less than 2,000 dan who disobeyed orders were executed. Baoshengzhi inspected Beiyang and wanted to kill Wang Xin. Wang Xin had undressed and was lying on the chopping board under the guillotine. Gongxin raised his head and said to Baoshengzhi: You have the power of life and death and are powerful in the county. Killing another Wang Xin now will not increase your prestige. It is better to be lenient according to the situation to show your kindness and mercy. Let me try my best to repay you. Bao Shengzhi admired what he said and forgave him without killing him. Therefore, Bao Shengzhi and Wang Xin became close friends. After Shengzhi completed his mission and returned to Beijing, he recommended Wang Xin to the emperor. Emperor Wu recruited him to serve as the captain of Youfu, acting as Youfu Feng. Emperor Wu visited Saitong and Jiidi many times. When he passed through Diehuang, Tanqiu sent people to clean the palace, make the roads smooth, and set up curtains and curtains for comfort. Emperor Wu was very happy, commended Wang Xin, stopped the car, and changed Wang Xin's official position to a regular one, and he ruled for more than ten years. During the reign of Emperor Zhao, Wang Xin served as the imperial censor, succeeded Che Qianqiu as prime minister, and was named Marquis of Yichun.

Under Emperor Zhao, he succeeded Che Qianqiu as Chancellor and was titled Marquis of Yichun, dying the following year.

Yang Zhong's younger brother Yang Yun, named Ziyou, relied on Yang Zhong's official position and was appointed Lang Guan according to the Han Dynasty's son appointment system, filling the post of Chang Shiqi. Yang Yun's mother was Sima Qian's daughter. Yang Yun first read "Tai Shi Gong Ji" written by his grandfather, and was also familiar with "Spring and Autumn". Because of his talent, he is praised by people. He liked to make friends with handsome and outstanding Confucian scholars. He became famous in the court and was promoted to Zuocao.

source: Wei Qing, courtesy name Zhongqing. His father, Zheng Ji, was from Pingyang, Hedong Province. He served as a county official and worked as an errand in the Pingyang Hou family. Pingyang Hou Cao Shou married Princess Yang Xinchang, the sister of Emperor Mowu. Zheng Ji had an affair with his master's servant Wei Wei and gave birth to Wei Qing. Wei Qing had an elder brother, Wei Changjun, and an elder sister, Wei Zifu. Wei Zifu was favored by Emperor Wu in Princess Pingyang's family, so Wei Qing assumed the surname Wei. Wei's eldest daughter is Junru, her second daughter is Shaoer, and her third daughter is Wei Zifu. Wei Zifu's younger brother Bu Guang took the surname Wei. Wei Qing was considered a member of Pingyang Hou's family and returned to his father's home when he was a child. His father made him herd sheep, and his aunt's sons treated him as a slave and were not counted among their brothers. Wei Qing once followed someone to the prisoner's room in Ganquan Palace. A prisoner who was being tortured came to him and said, "You are a noble person. If you become an official, you can become a marquis." Wei Qing smiled and said: "A son born from a slave would be very satisfied if he could not be beaten or scolded. How could there be such a good thing as becoming a prince?" When Wei Qing grew up, he became a knight of the Pingyang Hou family and followed Princess Pingyang. In the spring of the second year of Jianyuan, Wei Qing's sister Wei Zifu entered the palace and was favored by the emperor. Queen Chen is the daughter of the eldest princess. She has no son and is jealous of others. The eldest princess heard that Wei Zifu was favored and was pregnant. She was jealous of her and sent people to arrest Wei Qing. Wei Qing was working as an errand in Jianzhang Palace at that time and was not yet famous. The eldest princess caught Wei Qing, imprisoned him, and wanted to kill him. Wei Qing's friend Qi Lang Gongsun Ao and the warriors went to snatch him out, and Wei Qing avoided death. When the emperor heard about this, he summoned Wei Qing and asked him to be the eunuch of Jianzhang Palace and serve as a minister. When his half-brothers became prominent, the rewards amounted to thousands of gold in a few days. Jun Ru married Grand Servant Sun He as his wife. Wei Shaoer originally had an affair with Chen Zhang, and the emperor summoned Chen Zhang to make him an official. Gongsun Ao thus became more prominent. Wei Zifu became the emperor's wife. Wei Qing became a doctor in Taizhong. In the sixth year of Yuanguang, Wei Qing served as the cavalry general and attacked the Xiongnu and sent troops to Shanggu County; Gongsun He served as the light chariot general and left Yunzhong County; Taizhong doctor Gongsun Ao served as the cavalry general and left Dai County; Wei Wei Li Guang served as the Xiaocai general and left Yanmen County. Each army has one cavalry. Wei Qing marched to Longcheng and annihilated hundreds of enemy troops. The cavalry general Gongsun Ao lost 7,000 cavalry, and the guard Li Guang was captured alive by the enemy, but fortunately escaped. Both of them were sentenced to death and made atonement by becoming commoners. Gongsun He also had no military exploits. Only Wei Qing conferred the title of Marquis of Guannei. After that, the Huns continued to invade the borders. The incident is recorded in "The Biography of the Huns". In the spring of the first year of Yuanshuo, Mrs. Wei gave birth to a son and was made queen.

A prisoner once prophesied he would become a marquis, but Wei Qing dismissed this, content to avoid beatings. He later became a knight for the Pingyang Hou family. source: In the autumn of this year, Wei Qing led 30,000 cavalry to attack the Xiongnu and sent troops to Yanmen Pass. Li Xi sent troops to replace the county. Thirty-eight hundred households were assigned the title of Marquis of Changping to Wei Qing.
